hints: The shoelace formula calculates polygon area from consecutive vertices.
Sum x_i y_(i+1)-y_i x_(i+1), including the closing edge.
Take the absolute value; this is already twice the area.
analogy: Each directed edge contributes a signed strip; overlaps cancel and leave the polygon's area.
example: The triangle (0,0),(2,0),(0,3) has area 3, so the requested output is 6.
algorithm: Traverse all edges cyclically and sum x_i*y_next-y_i*x_next. Print the absolute value of this sum using an integer type wide enough for the accumulated products.
correctness: The shoelace formula gives signed twice-area for either orientation. Taking the absolute value removes the orientation and preserves the requested integer.
complexity: For n vertices, O(n) time and O(n) space if storing vertices, or O(1) extra space when streaming.
